subject: c-fo-act
title: C.FO.ACT.------TR.
description: Diagram in EXT.F(II)-10. Note this is a *tree* diagram (not crossing) — structurally distinct: a sparse, focused structure compared to the dense crossings throughout the section. C-FO-ACT (composite focused activism) is the trunk, with branches: → PHY-U-C (physical universe context) → DYM-F (dynamic functionalism); → (R)INT (the reality of intention) → TR (transformation); ← (R)PART (the reality of participation feeding C-FO-ACT, the only inverse direction). Structural argument: composite focused activism produces, through its primary branches, *only two* downstream lines — physical-universe-context-into-dynamic-functionalism, and the-reality-of-intention-into-transformation. The reality of participation is the only upstream feed. The diagram is starkly sparse compared to the crossing-diagram complexity dominating EXT.F(II): it is Braxton's structural specification that composite focused activism, when it actually works, is *minimal* — it requires only real participation as input, and produces only the dynamic-functionalism path and the transformation path as outputs. Read against the section: this is the tree-form diagram of what the AACM-style movements have demonstrated structurally — that composite focused activism's productive form is uncluttered, requiring only real participation upstream and producing only two downstream chains, with transformation reachable through real intention as the singular productive route.
